def: The legacy Compute Engine method to limit a VM. Both the access scopes and the IAM roles must allow a request, so set the cloud-platform scope and control access with IAM roles.
An opaque OAuth 2.0 token that calls Google APIs, such as Cloud Storage or Pub/Sub. It lasts 1 hour by default, and it cannot call a private Cloud Run service, which needs an ID token.

The time that a subscriber has to acknowledge a Pub/Sub message before redelivery: 10 seconds by default, and 10 to 600 seconds. High-level client libraries extend it for each message, by default for up to an hour.

The strategy that the authentication libraries use to find credentials. It checks GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, then the local file from gcloud auth application-default login, then the attached service account.
A Gemini Code Assist mode (Preview) that completes multi-step tasks with built-in tools and MCP servers. It asks before it changes files or resources, unless you allow the tool always.

Google Cloud's AI platform (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, formerly Vertex AI) that serves the Gemini API. A principal needs aiplatform.endpoints.predict to send prompts, for example through the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform User role.
One of the API design rules that Google follows for its own Cloud APIs. For example, AIP-121 says that an API that copies the database schema is an anti-pattern.
A Cloud Monitoring policy that fires on a metric condition, such as a threshold or an absence, or on a message in a log entry. A SQL-based policy (Public Preview) watches the results of a SQL query.
The IAM policy on a resource that grants roles to principals. Resources inherit allow policies, so a role on a project applies to every resource in the project.
A PostgreSQL-compatible database (AlloyDB for PostgreSQL) for demanding transactional workloads and for analytics on live transactional data. A cluster stores 16 TiB by default and up to 128 TiB.
The AlloyDB program that authorizes connections with IAM and encrypts the traffic. It finds credentials with ADC and uses the network path that already exists.
An API Gateway resource that holds your uploaded OpenAPI document or gRPC definition. It cannot change, so a new upload creates a new API config.

A fully managed, pay-per-use gateway for serverless backends that you configure with an OpenAPI document. A gateway is regional and hosts exactly one API config, and it calls the backend with an ID token for its service account.
A string that identifies a Google Cloud project for quota, billing, and monitoring. It does not identify a user or a service, so it is less secure than a token.
An Apigee bundle of operations on API proxies, with an optional quota, that app developers register for. Apigee provisions API keys for API products, not for API proxies.
An Apigee resource between clients and a backend. Its ProxyEndpoint is the URL that clients call and usually holds the security and rate-limit policies, and its TargetEndpoint calls the backend.
Google Cloud's native API management platform. It puts an API proxy layer with policies between clients and backends, and it has developer portals, API products, and monetization.
A Google Cloud platform that runs apps in the standard environment and the flexible environment. Google recommends Cloud Run as the preferred alternative for new users and for new projects.
Bigtable settings, one for each workload, that set how requests route to the clusters: single-cluster routing or multi-cluster routing. The code selects the app profile when it opens the table.
Google Cloud's Layer 7 proxy load balancer for HTTP and HTTPS (formerly HTTP(S) Load Balancing). The global external type has one anycast IP address for backends in many regions.
aws: Elastic Load Balancing Application Load Balancer

def: The service (formerly Container Analysis) that scans each new image that you push to Artifact Registry, once per digest. It updates the results with new vulnerability data, but they become stale after 30 days without a pull.

Google Cloud's recommended registry for container images and language packages. Each repository has one format and one mode, for example standard, remote, or virtual, and you cannot change the mode later.

A delivery guarantee where the same data can arrive more than once, so the receiver must handle duplicates. It is the Pub/Sub default, and a duplicate can also arrive after a successful acknowledgment.
A user-managed service account that you attach to a resource, such as a Cloud Run service or a VM. ADC gets its credentials from the metadata server, and Google lists this method as the most secure.
A signature over an image digest that Binary Authorization checks at deploy time. Cloud Build signs one at build time, so it exists only after the build completes.
A Binary Authorization resource that holds the public key that verifies attestations. Require the built-by-cloud-build attestor to deploy only images that Cloud Build built.

A CEL expression on a Workload Identity Federation provider that accepts or rejects each credential. A GitHub provider needs one for your organization, because tokens from other organizations share the issuer.
The OAuth 2.0 flow for web server apps. After the user gives consent, the app exchanges the returned code for an access token, and access_type=offline also returns a refresh token.
A Cloud Service Mesh policy that controls which workload identities can send which requests. Without policies, the mesh allows all requests, and it evaluates DENY policies before ALLOW policies.
The IP address ranges that can connect to a Cloud SQL public IP address. A Cloud SQL connector needs no authorized networks, so use a connector for clients with ephemeral IP addresses.
A Cloud Run option that lets Google patch the operating system and language runtime of a running service. You do not rebuild or redeploy, and Cloud Run does not create a new revision.
The path that routes requests to an Apigee API proxy, and that can hold the major version. It must be unique within an environment.
The legacy Owner, Editor, and Viewer roles, with thousands of permissions. They do not accept IAM Conditions, and they do not belong in production.
An asynchronous Agent Platform job for up to 200,000 requests, at 50% less than real-time inference. A job can wait in the queue for up to 72 hours, so it is not for a chat feature.
One HTTP request that sends many API calls. A batch of n calls counts as n requests toward your usage limit, and the server can run the calls in any order.
A Firestore set of writes that is atomic and needs no reads. Use it instead of a transaction when the writes do not depend on reads.

A serverless analytics platform with columnar storage that queries terabytes in seconds. A table runs at most 2 UPDATE, DELETE, or MERGE statements at the same time, so it is not a database for app transactions.
A Pub/Sub subscription that writes each message to an existing BigQuery table, with no subscriber code and no Dataflow job. It supports only at-least-once delivery.

A wide-column NoSQL database (formerly Cloud Bigtable) for terabytes or petabytes of single-keyed data, with high throughput at low latency. The row key is the only index, and transactions work only within a single row.
A deploy-time control on GKE and Cloud Run that blocks images without the attestations that the policy requires. It does not stop Pods that already run, and on GKE you must deploy by digest.
Your Cloud Run functions code that Identity Platform runs during sign-up and sign-in. It must respond within seven seconds, and it applies to all users in the project, also users in tenants.
A release that runs a second full set of instances with the new version and then switches all traffic. Rollback is a simple reversal of the switch, but it uses twice the resources.
A Binary Authorization option that deploys a blocked image in an emergency. It always writes an audit log entry, so alert on breakglass events.
A permanent lock on a bucket retention policy. You can then increase the period but not reduce or remove it, and Cloud Storage adds a lien that blocks project deletion.

Verifiable metadata about a build, such as image digests, source locations, build arguments, and build duration. Cloud Build generates it only for images that the images field pushes to Artifact Registry.
A Cloud Build rule that starts builds on repository events, manual runs, Pub/Sub messages, or webhooks. Each trigger needs a service account with only the roles that its build needs.
Google Cloud's tool that builds an image from source code and its dependency file, with no Dockerfile. The builder detects the language and uses a secure base image that Google manages.

The removal of content from a cache before it expires. Cloud CDN accepts up to 500 invalidation requests per minute, and invalidation does not clear browser caches, so Google recommends versioned URLs instead.
A caching pattern where the app reads the cache first and returns the value on a hit. On a miss, the app reads the database, writes the value to the cache with a TTL, and returns it.

A release that sends a small percentage of traffic to the new version, checks it, and then increases the percentage. Compare the canary with the control, because the error rate of the whole service hides canary errors.
The expression language of IAM Conditions. A CEL expression can use resource attributes, such as the resource type and name, and request attributes, such as the date and time.
A pattern where each service reacts to events, and no service controls the flow. In orchestration, a central service controls the flow.
An Artifact Registry rule that deletes old artifact versions, or keeps matching ones. It applies only to standard repositories, and when both kinds match, the keep policy wins.

A service that runs each build step as a Docker container, one after the other on one machine by default. A triggered build runs as the service account on the trigger, not the one in the build config.

Google's content delivery network, which caches responses at Google edge locations. It works only with the global external and classic Application Load Balancers, on a backend service or backend bucket.
The recommended libraries to call Google Cloud APIs from code. They find credentials with ADC, and unlike the older Google API Client Libraries, they can use gRPC for some APIs.
An extension for VS Code and JetBrains IDEs, also built into the Cloud Shell Editor. It supports GKE and Cloud Run development, Secret Manager, and the Cloud APIs.
aws: AWS Toolkit for VS Code and JetBrains

def: A service that delivers a release to a series of targets, such as GKE and Cloud Run, in a promotion sequence. A rollback is a new rollout of the last successful release.
An API management product that uses ESPv2, a proxy that you deploy and operate yourself. It fits when the gateway must run next to your app or in your private network.
Google Cloud's key management service, with key rings, keys, and key versions. Its Encrypt method accepts at most 64 KiB, and the Cloud KMS Admin role cannot encrypt or decrypt.
Google Cloud's service for timestamped log entries. Cloud Run and GKE collect JSON lines from stdout and stderr automatically, and special JSON fields set the severity, labels, and trace.
Google Cloud's service for metric time series, uptime checks, alerting policies, and SLOs. Log-based metrics turn log entries into Cloud Monitoring metrics without code changes.

A service that continuously collects CPU and memory-allocation data from production code with low overhead. You add a language-specific agent library, and a user-created service account needs the Cloud Profiler Agent role.
A serverless platform that runs containers as services, jobs, and worker pools. One instance serves many requests at the same time, and a service scales to zero.

A Cloud Run service that you deploy from function source code (formerly Cloud Functions 2nd gen). Cloud Run builds the function into a container, so the function gets service features such as Direct VPC and GPUs.
The role (roles/run.invoker) that lets a principal call a private Cloud Run service. Grant it to the caller's service account on the receiving service, not on the project and not to allUsers.
A Cloud Run resource that runs tasks to completion and gets no inbound traffic. A task can run for up to 168 hours (7 days), and an execution succeeds only when all its tasks succeed.
A service that runs cron jobs on a unix-cron schedule, each with one target: an HTTP endpoint, a Pub/Sub topic, or an App Engine app. A job does not retry by default.

Google's service mesh (formerly Anthos Service Mesh and Traffic Director). On GKE it runs a sidecar proxy next to each workload, uses mTLS between services, and controls access with authorization policies.
A terminal and an editor in the browser, on a VM that Google owns, with the gcloud CLI installed. Only the 5 GB $HOME directory persists, and non-interactive sessions end after 40 minutes.
Google Cloud's managed MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server service, the start point for a general-purpose app. An instance with dedicated cores stores up to 64 TB, and its read replicas are read-only.
A program that authorizes Cloud SQL connections with IAM and encrypts them. It does not create a network path or pool connections, and the docs prefer a Language Connector when your language has one.
Google Cloud's object storage, with no lower or upper capacity limit. An object can be 5 TiB, but you can write to one object name only once per second.
The adapter behind Cloud Storage volume mounts, which show the objects in a bucket as local files, for example in Cloud Run. It has no file locking, so the last write wins.
A queue service for explicit invocation: the producer names the HTTP target of each task, and the queue sets the dispatch rate and retries. Delivery is at least once, so handlers must be idempotent.
Google Cloud's service for the spans of a request across services. Cloud Run creates request traces automatically, but Cloud Trace itself does not propagate trace context.

A service that runs each development workstation on a Compute Engine VM in your project and VPC network. A workstation configuration is the template, and a change applies at the next start of each workstation.
A CNCF specification that describes event data in a common way. Eventarc sends each event as an HTTP POST to the receiver's root path, with the attributes in ce- headers and the data in the body.
The GKE Standard autoscaler that adds nodes when GKE cannot schedule Pods. It decides from Pod requests, not from actual use.

Cloud KMS keys that you control and that a Google Cloud service uses for server-side envelope encryption. Grant the Encrypter/Decrypter role to the service agent, not to the user who creates the resource.

A Gemini Code Assist Enterprise feature that indexes your private GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket repositories as context. The index refreshes every 24 hours, and only .aiexclude excludes files from it.

An AlloyDB feature, also in some Spanner editions, that keeps selected columns in memory in a column format. It speeds up scans, joins, and aggregates, but frequent updates invalidate the column data.

A Cloud Build pull request trigger setting that needs a /gcbrun comment from an owner or collaborator before a build runs. Without it, any user with read access to a public repository can run code in your build.
A Spanner column that records the commit time of each transaction. As the first key part of a table or an index, it creates a hotspot, even at low write rates.
Google Cloud's VM service, with Linux or Windows images and predefined or custom machine types. Choose it when the OS, the kernel, or a software license is a requirement, for example for SAP HANA.
The registry that Artifact Registry replaced. It shut down on March 18, 2025, and you cannot write images to it.
The rules that a Cloud Run container must follow. For example, it listens on 0.0.0.0 at the PORT variable, runs Linux x86_64 code, and starts to listen within 4 minutes.
GKE load balancing that sends traffic directly to Pod IP addresses through NEGs, so traffic skips the node and kube-proxy. Gateway and Ingress use it, but LoadBalancer Services do not.
A Gemini feature that reduces the cost and latency of requests that repeat the same large content. Implicit caching is on by default, and an explicit cache lasts 60 minutes by default.
A Binary Authorization feature (Preview) that checks running GKE Pods against check-based platform policies at least every 24 hours. It logs violations but does not stop Pods.
A discount for a commitment to use resources. Compute flexible commitments cover Compute Engine, GKE, and Cloud Run, and resource-based CUDs cover Compute Engine only, in one region.

An audience value, other than the service URL, that a Cloud Run service accepts in the aud claim of an ID token. Configure one for a custom domain or a load balancer, because a custom domain is not a valid audience.
An IAM role with permissions that you choose and maintain. Use it when every predefined role with the permission grants too much, and create it only at the organization or project level.
A service that runs data pipelines, for custom sources or for complex transforms, windows, and aggregation before a write. Its Pub/Sub to BigQuery template enforces exactly-once delivery by default.
aws: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink

def: A Pub/Sub topic, set on a subscription, that receives the messages that subscribers cannot acknowledge. The Pub/Sub service agent needs publisher and subscriber roles, and the topic needs its own subscription.
A service account that some services create when you enable their API. It can get the Editor role, and Cloud Run uses the Compute Engine default service account when you specify no service account.
The Storage Write API stream that you do not create. Rows are visible at once, and delivery is at-least-once, so use committed type with offsets for exactly-once delivery.
The key that encrypts the data in envelope encryption. Generate a new DEK locally for each write, and store only the DEK that the KEK wraps.
An Eventarc event that a Google service sends directly, not through a Cloud Audit Logs entry. Use it when it exists, because it has lower latency, a typed format, and no audit log cost.

The recommended way to send Cloud Run traffic to internal IP addresses, for example to Memorystore. It is for outbound traffic only, and instances get IP addresses from your subnet, which must be /26 or larger.
A Firestore counter document with a subcollection of shards, for a count that changes at a high rate. Write throughput grows with the number of shards, but each read of the total reads every shard.
A Cloud Run feature (Preview) that maps a custom domain to a service. Google does not recommend it for production, so use a global external Application Load Balancer instead.
A policy mode that does not deny requests and only writes the violations to audit logs. Google recommends that you test all policy changes in this mode first.
Encryption where a local data encryption key (DEK) encrypts the data and a key encryption key (KEK) in Cloud KMS wraps the DEK. Use it for data over the 64 KiB limit of Cloud KMS.
A service that groups error events from log entries that contain a stack trace, and from its API and client libraries. It cannot analyze log entries in log buckets that use CMEK.
A value that changes when a resource changes. With If-None-Match, a cached ETag gives 304 Not Modified, and with If-Match, an old ETag gives 412 Precondition Failed.
An object hold that blocks deletion. When you release it, the retention period starts again for that object, so it fits a rule such as N years after an event.

A service that routes events from providers to destinations and delivers each event as an HTTP request in the CloudEvents format. Eventarc Standard routes with triggers, and Eventarc Advanced adds a central bus.

An Eventarc rule that delivers matching events as HTTP POST requests to a destination, such as a Cloud Run service in the same project. Its subscription has a 10-second acknowledgment deadline by default, and Google recommends 600 seconds.
A model where a write to one copy becomes readable from the other copies only after replication. Bigtable replication between clusters and Cloud Storage access changes have eventual consistency.

A Pub/Sub subscription setting for an application that cannot accept any duplicate. Only pull subscriptions support it, and a publisher retry can still store the same data twice, with different message IDs.
One of two Cloud Run runtime types, at the same price. The first generation uses gVisor and starts fast, and the second generation is a microVM with full Linux compatibility and NFS support.
A pattern where the producer names the endpoint for each task, as in Cloud Tasks. In implicit invocation, as in Pub/Sub, the publisher does not know the subscribers.
A retry method that doubles the wait after each failure, up to a maximum backoff, such as 32 or 64 seconds. Add jitter to each wait, and stop retrying after a deadline.
A metric from outside the cluster that the HPA can scale on, such as a Pub/Sub backlog in Cloud Monitoring. An External metric can also scale a workload up from zero replicas.
A managed NFS file server. VMs, GKE clusters, and Cloud Run services can use one file system at the same time.
A sign-in service that uses Identity Platform as its backend. SAML and OIDC providers, MFA, and tenants need an upgrade to Identity Platform, and the upgrade needs no app change.

A serverless document database that needs no capacity planning and scales automatically. It gives single-digit millisecond reads, ACID transactions, real-time listeners, and offline support for mobile apps.
A local Firestore that keeps data in memory and, in Native mode, does not check manual indexes. It also emulates Datastore mode with --database-mode=datastore-mode.

The Firestore data access mode (formerly Cloud Datastore) for legacy apps that depend on the Datastore API, such as App Engine apps. You select the mode when you create the database, and you cannot change it.
A Pub/Sub client library setting that limits the outstanding messages and bytes of a publisher or a subscriber. It is for temporary spikes, so add client instances for a lasting overload.
A Gemini feature where the model returns a function name and arguments, and your application runs the function and sends the result back. It cannot share a request with Grounding with Google Search.
An open source library that wraps one function in a local HTTP server on port 8080. Cloud Run uses it to wrap deployed functions.
Bigtable rules that delete cells in a column family by age, by number of versions, or by a combination. Deletion can take up to a week, so add a read filter that matches the rule.
The Kubernetes API that Google recommends for GKE load balancers. A Gateway defines where the load balancer listens, and an HTTPRoute sends requests to Services.
aws: Amazon EKS with an Ingress controller

def: The command-line tool of the Cloud SDK, also named the Google Cloud CLI. The gcloud auth login command gives credentials to the gcloud CLI only, and code that uses client libraries needs ADC.
A named set of gcloud CLI properties, such as the project and the account. A switch to another configuration does not change your local ADC file, so client library code keeps the same credentials.
The gemini command, which runs agent tasks from a terminal or Cloud Shell. It shares its quota with agent mode and uses a .geminiignore file to exclude files.
An AI assistant in the Google Cloud console (Preview). Do not enable it for projects with data residency or CMEK requirements.
aws: Amazon Q in the AWS console

def: A Gemini Cloud Assist feature (Preview) that looks at logs, metrics, and configurations to find probable root causes. Since April 10, 2026, only users with a Premium Support contract or account team access can run them.
An AI coding assistant for IDEs, the Cloud Shell Editor, and Cloud Workstations, with Standard and Enterprise editions. A user needs a license and the Gemini for Google Cloud User role.
aws: Amazon Q Developer in the IDE

def: A Gemini Code Assist product that reviews GitHub pull requests and gives each comment a severity: Critical, High, Medium, or Low. The default threshold is MEDIUM, so Low issues get no comment.

Google Cloud's Kubernetes service, best for complex microservices, stateful apps, and deep Kubernetes control. It charges a fee per cluster per hour in both modes, Autopilot and Standard, plus the compute.

The recommended GKE cluster mode for most production use cases. Autopilot configures nodes from your Pod resource requests, applies default requests when you set none, and rejects requests above the maximum.
A GKE feature that creates Application Load Balancers from Kubernetes Ingress resources. It is in maintenance mode with no new features, so Google recommends the Gateway API.
The GKE mode where you manage the node VMs and pay for them, plus the cluster fee. Use it only for a configuration that Autopilot blocks, such as privileged Pods or Windows Server containers.

An API endpoint that does not name a region, so Google chooses where to process the request. For Gemini, it gives higher availability and fewer 429 errors, but it does not meet data residency requirements.
The console area for the OAuth consent screen and OAuth clients. Its Audience page sets who can authorize the app: Internal (users in your organization) or External (any Google Account).
The SDK (google-genai) that is one interface for the Gemini Developer API and the Gemini API on Agent Platform. With a few exceptions, code for one runs on the other.
A Gemini feature that connects model output to sources that you can check, such as Google Search or Agent Search. It reduces hallucinations and gives links to the sources.

A configuration that keeps a service available during a failure, with resources in more than one zone or region. Cloud SQL HA fails over automatically to a standby in a second zone of the same region, so it protects against a zone outage only.
A Cloud Storage credential that signs S3-compatible requests to the XML API. The Cloud Storage tools do not create signed URLs from HMAC keys.
aws: S3-compatible requests signed with HMAC keys

def: A server or node that gets too large a share of the traffic. In Spanner, a first key part that always increases, such as a timestamp, sends every insert to the last split.

The GKE autoscaler that changes the number of Pods based on CPU or memory use, custom metrics, or external metrics. It does not add nodes, and a utilization target needs resource requests on the containers.
A mapping of each RPC to an HTTP method with the google.api.http annotation, so clients can use gRPC or JSON over HTTP. API Gateway and Cloud Endpoints can do it for you.
A Gateway API resource that sends requests from a Gateway to Services. Application developers create it, and it can match request headers and split traffic by weight.
Durable block storage for Compute Engine VMs and GKE clusters, with performance and capacity that scale separately. For redundancy across zones, use Hyperdisk Balanced High Availability.
Limits on a role binding, written as a CEL expression, for example an expiry time or a resource name prefix. A conditional binding does not override a binding of the same role without a condition.
A database login with a temporary OAuth 2.0 access token instead of a password. In automatic mode the connector refreshes the token, and the principal needs the Cloud SQL Instance User role.
An authorization layer that checks a user's identity and IAM role before a request reaches the app. Enable it directly on a Cloud Run service, and verify the signed JWT that it adds to each request.
aws: AWS Application Load Balancer with Cognito, and AWS Verified Access

def: A signed JWT that calls Cloud Run, Cloud Run functions, apps behind IAP, and APIs on API Gateway. Its aud claim names the receiver, and it cannot call a Google API.
The property of an operation that gives the same result when it runs more than once. Retry only idempotent operations, or conditionally idempotent operations that include their precondition.

Google Cloud's customer identity and access management (CIAM) platform. It adds MFA, blocking functions, SAML and OIDC providers, multi-tenancy, and an SLA to Firebase Authentication, which uses it as its backend.
The SHA-256 hash of an image manifest or index, which identifies one image version and cannot change. Deploy by digest when you must run exactly the image that you scanned or signed.

Cloud Run settings that control the network paths that can reach a service: all, internal-and-cloud-load-balancing, or internal. IAM authentication still applies on every path, and Google recommends both controls.

A Cloud Run billing setting (formerly CPU always allocated) that charges for the whole instance lifetime, with no per-request fee. It gives CPU outside requests, so use it for background work after the response.

A Spanner option that stores child rows with their parent row, and the child primary key starts with the parent primary key. It is permanent, and Google recommends interleaving or a foreign key for a relationship, not both.
A random fraction of a second that a client adds to each backoff wait. It stops many clients from retrying at the same time.
A signed token that carries claims, such as an ID token. Before you use any claim, validate the signature with the issuer's public keys, and check the issuer, the audience, and the expiry.
The Cloud KMS key that wraps the DEK in envelope encryption. The KEK never leaves Cloud KMS.
The creation of a new version of a Cloud KMS key. It does not re-encrypt existing data or disable old versions, and automatic rotation is for symmetric keys only.
The key material of a Cloud KMS key, numbered from 1. No one can view or export it, and a symmetric key encrypts with its primary version by default.
The Kubernetes identity that a Pod uses. With Workload Identity Federation for GKE, grant IAM roles to its principal identifier, so the Pod needs no service account key.

Cloud SQL and AlloyDB libraries for some languages, such as Java, Python, and Go, that authorize connections with IAM and encrypt the traffic. They do not create a network path, and the Cloud SQL docs prefer them to the Auth Proxy.
A probe that decides when to restart a container, for example after a deadlock. It must not check other services, such as a database, because a bad liveness probe causes cascading restarts.
A BigQuery batch job that loads data, for example from Cloud Storage. It is free with the shared slot pool, but a table allows 1,500 load jobs each day, failed jobs included.
A Kubernetes Service type that creates a passthrough Network Load Balancer, not an Application Load Balancer. For path-based HTTP routing, use a Gateway and an HTTPRoute.
Temporary block storage for Compute Engine VMs and GKE clusters. You lose its data when the VM stops or when you delete the VM, so do not use it for data that must survive.
A Cloud Monitoring metric from matching log entries, with no code change. A user-defined log-based metric counts only the entries that arrive after you create it.
The filter language of the Logs Explorer. NOT has the highest precedence, then OR, then AND, and lowercase and, or, and not are search terms.
The Cloud Logging page where you troubleshoot and explore log entries with the Logging query language. It does not aggregate, so use Observability Analytics to aggregate log data with SQL.
An object, google.longrunning.Operation, that a method returns when its work takes more than about 10 seconds. An HTTP 200 then means only that the server accepted the request.
A server-side connection pool for Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL on Enterprise Plus edition. It helps most with many short-lived connections or connection surges, for example from Cloud Run.
Google's Apache Airflow service (formerly Cloud Composer) for ETL or ELT pipelines as Python DAGs. Its latency is in seconds, so it is not for low-latency service orchestration.
Google's managed Prometheus service, whose managed collection Google recommends for all Kubernetes environments. Google also recommends it to create and manage custom metrics.
A Firestore index (formerly composite index) that you create for a range filter or a sort combined with another field. The error for a missing index has a link that creates it.
A Cloud Run setting that limits cost and the number of connections to a backend, such as a database. The default is 100 instances per revision.
An open source protocol that standardizes how AI applications connect to data sources. An MCP server exposes tools, prompts, and resources, through stdio on your machine or HTTP for a remote server.

Google Cloud's in-memory cache service: Memorystore for Valkey, Redis Cluster, Redis, and Memcached, which is deprecated. Memorystore for Redis uses private IP addresses, so Cloud Run reaches it through the VPC network.
A Memorystore product for one Redis node of up to 300 GB. It supports RDB snapshots but not AOF, and only the Standard Tier has replication and automatic failover.
A Memorystore product with Redis shards, each with 0 to 5 replicas in other zones. It scales without downtime, has a 99.99% SLA, and supports AOF or RDB persistence.
The Memorystore product that Google recommends instead of the deprecated Memorystore for Memcached. It scales without downtime, has a 99.99% SLA, and supports AOF or RDB persistence.
The source of credentials for the attached service account on Google Cloud. ADC gets tokens from it, and it gives ID tokens for the attached service account, not for user credentials.
A group of identical Compute Engine VMs. A regional MIG spreads the VMs across zones, and Google recommends it over a zonal MIG.
A Cloud Run setting that keeps instances warm to reduce cold starts. You pay for the idle instances, and Google recommends at least 3 for high availability.

TLS that authenticates and encrypts the traffic between services. In Cloud Service Mesh, auto mTLS is on by default, but services also accept plaintext until a PeerAuthentication policy sets STRICT mode.

A Bigtable app profile routing that sends requests to any cluster and fails over automatically to the nearest available cluster. Its consistency is eventual, and it never allows single-row transactions.
A write operation in a database API. In Spanner, mutations are not visible until the commit, so do not mix them with DML in one transaction.
A load balancer backend type. A serverless NEG points to a Cloud Run service, and GKE container-native load balancing uses GCE_VM_IP_PORT NEGs to reach Pod IP addresses.
A subscriber response that makes Pub/Sub redeliver a message at once, unless a retry policy sets a delay. Nack a message that the subscriber cannot process now, so that Pub/Sub does not lose it.

Google Cloud's Layer 4 load balancer, as a proxy for TCP or as a passthrough for TCP, UDP, and other IP protocols. A passthrough load balancer keeps the client source IP, and backends reply to clients directly.
aws: Elastic Load Balancing Network Load Balancer

def: A Kubernetes rule that selects Pods by label and lists the Pods that can connect to them or that they can connect to. It only allows or blocks connections, and a Standard cluster without a network plugin ignores it.

The service account that GKE nodes run as, by default the Compute Engine default service account. Nodes pull images as this account, so for a repository in another project, grant Artifact Registry Reader to it, not to the Pod's ServiceAccount.

Cloud Storage rules that act on the objects that match their conditions, for example with Delete or SetStorageClass. Each rule has exactly one action, and actions run asynchronously, so a change can take up to 24 hours.
A Cloud Storage bucket setting that keeps earlier versions as noncurrent objects, which you can read by generation number. It is off by default and does not protect against bucket deletion.
The Cloud Logging feature (formerly Log Analytics) that runs SQL on upgraded log buckets and can join log and trace data. Use it to aggregate log data, which the Logs Explorer cannot do.
An identity protocol that issues ID tokens. Sign In With Google uses OAuth 2.0 and OIDC, and Identity Platform can sign in users through OIDC providers.
An Artifact Analysis feature that scans an image when you run a command, also a local image. Use it in a build to stop severe vulnerabilities, but Artifact Analysis does not update its results later.
A vendor-neutral framework for logs, metrics, and traces, which Google recommends instead of product-specific APIs. Export with OTLP, through a collector where the environment supports one.
A process that receives telemetry from apps and exports it, for example to the Telemetry API. On Cloud Run, run it as a sidecar with instance-based billing.
A pattern where a central service, such as Workflows, controls the flow between services. In choreography, each service reacts to events instead.
A Pub/Sub message value that keeps the order of messages with the same key, not across the topic. You must enable message ordering when you create the subscription.

A service that sets constraints on an organization, folder, or project, and descendant resources inherit them. IAM decides who can act, and an organization policy decides which configurations it allows.
The OpenTelemetry format for logs, metrics, and traces. The Telemetry API accepts OTLP data directly.

A Cloud Storage upload of up to 32 chunks as temporary objects, which a compose request joins. Do not use it with a retention policy, because the temporary objects cannot be deleted until they meet the retention period.
A response with only the fields that you ask for, through the fields system parameter or the X-Goog-FieldMask header. It changes only the response, so use PATCH to make an update request smaller.
A Spanner DML mode that runs large UPDATE and DELETE statements without transaction limits. It has no commit or rollback, so do not use it for an all-or-nothing change.
A Kubernetes object that limits voluntary disruptions, such as node drains. It does not limit a Deployment rolling update, so use maxUnavailable for that.
Durable block storage for Compute Engine VMs and GKE Pods, from 10 GiB to 64 TiB per disk. A zonal disk stays in one zone, so use regional Persistent Disk for redundancy across zones.

A request condition that stops race conditions, such as ifGenerationMatch=0, which writes a Cloud Storage object only if no live version exists. A failed precondition returns 412 Precondition Failed, and a precondition also makes a retry safe.
An IAM role that Google maintains and updates when it adds features. It is the default choice, so grant it on the lowest resource that the task needs.
A subnet setting that lets VMs without external IP addresses call Google APIs and run.app URLs. It has no effect on VMs with external IP addresses.
A Cloud Build pool that can reach private resources in a VPC network through VPC peering, and that supports VPC Service Controls. The default pool cannot reach private resources.
A private access option with an internal IP address that you choose, for Google APIs or for a service that another VPC network publishes. It uses NAT, so the networks need no IP address coordination.
A private access option that uses VPC Network Peering with an allocated range. It reaches Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Memorystore for Redis, or Filestore by internal IP address, but not Google APIs.
Gemini capacity that you buy. Requests over the purchase run as pay-as-you-go by default, and its 429 errors usually mean that you used all the purchased capacity.

An asynchronous messaging service that decouples the services that produce messages from the services that process them. Each subscription gets a copy of every message, and the default delivery is at-least-once, with no ordering.
aws: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon MQ

def: A local Pub/Sub that works only with the Cloud Client Libraries, not with the console or gcloud pubsub commands. Its port can change at each start, so run env-init again.
A deprecated Pub/Sub service that Google turns down on January 31, 2027. Do not use it in a new design.
A Cloud Storage setting or organization policy that blocks access through allUsers and allAuthenticatedUsers, also on existing buckets. Signed URLs still work.
aws: Public access settings for Amazon S3

def: A Pub/Sub subscription where the subscriber client requests messages and controls the rate. Only pull subscriptions support exactly-once delivery.

A Pub/Sub subscription that sends each message as an HTTP POST request to an endpoint, such as a Cloud Run service. The endpoint acknowledges with HTTP 102, 200, 201, 202, or 204, and any other code is a negative acknowledgment.

The project that a client-based API uses for quota. Set it for user credentials with x-goog-user-project or gcloud auth application-default set-quota-project, but a resource-based API always uses the resource's project.
A set of read nodes in AlloyDB, up to 20 per cluster, and in Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus edition. It can return stale data, so read from the primary instance when the code must see its own write.
A read-only copy of a Cloud SQL instance that moves read load off the primary instance. It can lag, it gives no failover, and it becomes a primary only when you promote it.
A Spanner transaction that takes no locks and can run on any replica. Use it, or a single read, for reads, and use a read-write transaction only when you must write.
A locking Spanner transaction for reads and writes that must be atomic. Keep it short, because long-held locks increase contention, deadlocks, and aborts.
A probe that decides when a container can take traffic. A failure removes the Pod from the Service endpoints, but the container continues to run.
A token that gets new access tokens or ID tokens, so a session can last long. Ask for it with access_type=offline, and keep it in secure long-term storage.

An API endpoint that names a region, so you control where Google processes the request. A SERVICE.REGION.rep.googleapis.com endpoint also ends TLS in that region, and it works only with resources in that region.
The default Cloud Run billing setting (formerly CPU only allocated during request processing). Cloud Run allocates CPU only during requests, so it does not support work after the response.
match: CPU only allocated during request processing

def: A Cloud Storage upload where a first request starts a session and the data goes to the session URI. It suits most cases and large files, and it costs one extra HTTP request.
A minimum age for all objects in a Cloud Storage bucket. A request to delete or replace a younger object fails, and the policy also applies to the objects that are already in the bucket.

A name that gives a Cloud Run revision its own URL, so you can test the revision before it gets traffic. With revision-level minimum instances, a tag keeps those instances running, and you pay for them.
IAM recommender suggestions to revoke or replace a role, based on the permissions that a principal used in the last 90 days. Except for service agents, a recommendation never increases access.
An update that replaces a subset of instances, then more, until all run the new version. A GKE Deployment controls it with maxSurge and maxUnavailable, which both default to 25%.
A Secret Manager setting that only sends a SECRET_ROTATE message to Pub/Sub on a schedule. Your own subscriber creates the new credential and adds the new version.
The only index of a Bigtable table, and rows sort by the bytes of the key. Design it for your queries, and put a high-cardinality value, not a timestamp, first.
The maximum time period in which data can be lost. A smaller RPO costs more.
The maximum time that an app can be offline. A smaller RTO costs more, and a near-zero RTO needs synchronous data replication.

Gemini filters that block harmful prompts and responses but do not change how the model behaves. A blocked response has empty content and a finish_reason, and the default threshold is OFF for gemini-3.5-flash and later.
A service that stores secrets as numbered, immutable versions. Grant the Secret Accessor role on one secret, and in production reference a version number, not the latest alias.
The recommended GKE add-on that mounts Secret Manager secrets as in-memory files in Pods through a CSI volume. It needs Workload Identity Federation for GKE.
Google Cloud's risk management service. It collects findings, which are records of threats or other issues, from its built-in services, integrated Google Cloud services, and third-party tools.
aws: Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub, AWS Config

def: A load balancer backend for one Cloud Run service or function in the same region. Only Application Load Balancers support it, and it has no health checks and no load balancer session affinity.
A way to send Cloud Run traffic to a VPC network through a connector, which adds connector VM charges. Compared with Direct VPC egress, it has higher latency but uses fewer IP addresses.
A Google Cloud identity that a workload uses. It is a principal that gets roles, and also a resource that other principals get roles on, such as the permission to attach it.

The use of short-lived credentials of a service account, with no key. The caller needs the Service Account Token Creator role on the service account, also as project Owner, and most audit logs show both identities.
A key file for a service account. A leaked key works without 2-step verification, so use an attached service account or Workload Identity Federation instead.

term: Service Account OpenID Connect Identity Token Creator
def: The role (roles/iam.serviceAccountOpenIdTokenCreator) that lets a principal create only ID tokens for a service account. Service Account Token Creator also creates access tokens.
match: Service Account OpenID Connect Identity Token Creator

def: The role (roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator) that lets a principal create access tokens and ID tokens for a service account and sign blobs and JWTs. Grant it on one service account, not on the project.

The role (roles/iam.serviceAccountUser) with the actAs permission, which lets a principal attach a service account to a resource. It does not allow impersonation, which needs Service Account Token Creator.
A service account that Google creates and manages, so that a service can act on your behalf. Do not revoke its roles unless a role recommendation suggests it, or the service stops working.
A Cloud Run feature that moves load balancer traffic away from an unhealthy region. A regional service is healthy when 60% or more of its instances pass their readiness probes.
The service account that a Cloud Run service runs as. When you specify no service account, Cloud Run uses the Compute Engine default service account, so attach a dedicated one.
The API that lists, enables, and disables services in a project. A call to a disabled service fails with SERVICE_DISABLED, so enable it in the project that the error names.
A load balancer setting that sends the requests of one client to the same backend. It is best effort and not for authentication, and a serverless NEG does not support it.
A helper container that runs next to the app container and shares its network, such as a proxy or a monitoring agent. A Cloud Run instance can have up to 10 containers, with one ingress container.
A signed set of conditions for an HTML form upload to Cloud Storage, because HTML forms do not support signed URLs. It also controls the size and content type of the upload.
A URL that gives anyone who has it time-limited access to one Cloud Storage resource, with no account. A V4 signed URL is valid for at most 7 days and works only with XML API endpoints.
A Bigtable app profile routing that sends requests to one cluster, with manual failover. It gives read-your-writes consistency and is the only routing that allows single-row transactions.
A framework of build maturity levels, where each level adds requirements to the level below it. Cloud Build can generate SLSA level 3 provenance for container images.

A Cloud Storage feature, on by default for 7 days, that keeps deleted and overwritten objects and deleted buckets. Google recommends it over Object Versioning to protect against accidental or malicious deletion.

A Cloud Run deploy with --source that builds the image with Cloud Build and buildpacks, or with your Dockerfile, and needs no local Docker. It stores the image in the cloud-run-source-deploy repository.
The record of one operation in a trace, with a name, a status, and a start and end time. Each span has its own span ID and the ID of its parent span, and the root span has no parent.

A relational database (formerly Cloud Spanner) that scales horizontally, for large-scale and strongly consistent workloads. Read and write throughput grow linearly with compute capacity, and each node holds 10 TiB of data.
aws: Amazon Aurora, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon Keyspaces, Amazon Neptune

def: An Apigee policy that limits the request rate to the backend for all clients, per second or per minute. Its counts are best effort, so use the Quota policy for contract limits.
Compute Engine VMs (the latest version of preemptible VMs) that cost up to 91% less. Compute Engine can preempt them at any time, and no SLA covers them, so use them for non-critical work.
A read at a past timestamp, which can lower latency when old data is acceptable. The Spanner and Firestore docs call a staleness of 15 seconds reasonable.
One of the five common API methods: Get, List, Create, Update, and Delete. Prefer them, because standard methods work in the most clients, such as CLIs, UIs, and SDKs.
A Cloud Run setting that adds CPU while an instance starts and for 10 seconds after. You pay for the boosted CPU, and the gcloud CLI turns it on by default for a new service.
A probe that checks whether the app has started. Until it succeeds, Kubernetes does not run the liveness and readiness probes, and Cloud Run adds a default TCP startup probe.

A Cloud Storage option that you pick by access frequency and storage time: Standard, Nearline, Coldline, or Archive. Colder classes cost less to store but add access costs, and even Archive data is available within milliseconds.
The BigQuery API for large reads, in parallel streams with column projection and row filters. It cannot read views, so query the view and then read the result table.
The BigQuery API for new streaming code, used over gRPC. It costs less than the legacy streaming API, and it supports exactly-once delivery with committed type and offsets.
The Pub/Sub pull API that the high-level client library uses, and that Google recommends for most subscribers. Use it instead of unary Pull for large volume or high throughput.
A read that returns all data that transactions committed before the read started. Spanner and Firestore give strong reads by default.
Logs written as JSON lines to stdout and stderr. Special fields such as severity, message, and logging.googleapis.com/trace move into the matching LogEntry fields.
A Gemini response in JSON that follows a schema. Set both response_schema and the application/json MIME type, because JSON mode without a schema is only a strong hint.
A collection inside a Firestore document, for data that grows, such as the messages of a chat room. When you delete the parent document, its subcollections stay.
A variable that Cloud Build replaces in steps and images at build time, such as $COMMIT_SHA in a triggered build. Write $$ for a shell variable, because Cloud Build reads $NAME as a substitution.
An automatic Compute Engine discount of up to 30% for VM use above 25% of the month. It does not apply to usage that a CUD covers, and E2 is not an eligible series.

A move of the primary role to a replica with zero data loss, in Cloud SQL and AlloyDB. Use it for disaster recovery drills and planned region moves, because promotion and replica failover can lose lagging data.
Instructions that steer how a Gemini model behaves, which filters cannot do. When a request uses a cache, put them in the cache, because the request cannot set them again.

The Google Cloud API (telemetry.googleapis.com) that accepts logs, metrics, and traces in OTLP format. The writer needs the Cloud Telemetry Writer role, a quota project, and Service Usage Consumer on it.

The trace ID, the parent span ID, and the sampling decision that a service sends to the next service. Each service must pass it on, in the W3C traceparent header where possible, because Cloud Trace does not propagate context.

A configuration that sends a percentage of requests to each version of an app. On Cloud Run, a split between revisions stays in place for all later deployments until you run update-traffic --to-latest.
A Cloud Storage option for dual-region buckets that copies 100% of new objects to the second region in 15 minutes. Default replication has an RPO of 12 hours.
A bucket setting where only IAM grants access, and ACL requests fail. After 90 consecutive days, you cannot disable it.
A service account that you create and manage, with one for each application. You can attach only user-managed service accounts to a VM.
An Apigee policy that checks that an API key belongs to an approved app for the API product. Apigee does not check keys automatically, so without a credential policy any caller gets through.
A GKE feature that sets the CPU and memory requests of Pods from historical usage, for long-running workloads with steady use. Do not combine it with the HPA on CPU or memory.
A service that puts a perimeter around Google Cloud services, such as Cloud Storage and BigQuery, to reduce the risk of data exfiltration. It adds a layer of defense to IAM and does not replace it.
A Security Command Center service that crawls public web apps on App Engine, GKE, and Compute Engine and reports issues such as XSS. It clicks buttons and submits forms, so scan a test environment.

A Cloud Run resource for always-on background work, such as Kafka or Pub/Sub pull consumers. It has no URL and no request-based autoscaling, and it does not start when its minimum instances value is 0.
A serverless orchestration platform that runs steps from a YAML or JSON definition. It has no charges while idle, and its HTTP calls carry no token until you add an auth block.

A feature that gives workloads on AWS, Azure, on premises, or in deployment pipelines access to Google Cloud without a service account key. The workload exchanges its own credential with the Security Token Service for a federated token.
aws: IAM OIDC identity provider for GitHub Actions

def: The recommended way for GKE workloads to call Google Cloud APIs, which the console still calls Workload Identity. The GKE metadata server exchanges a Kubernetes ServiceAccount token for a short-lived access token, so the code needs no change.
aws: IAM roles for service accounts on Amazon EKS

def: The role (roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser) that lets a federated identity impersonate a service account. Grant it on the service account only when an API has limits with direct resource access.

A Cloud Storage upload where parts go up in parallel and a final request joins them, compatible with Amazon S3 multipart uploads. It supports no preconditions, and you pay for unfinished parts until you remove them.
